requirements.summary: logrotate.d config written with 'daily' directive, syntax-checked via dry run with no errors, and confirmed wired into daily execution via /etc/cron.daily/logrotate -> /etc/logrotate.conf -> logrotate.d/*.
Config specifies rotate 7 + compress. A synthetic 9-day-old-rotation test plus a forced rotation directly demonstrated exactly 7 app.log-*.gz files retained with the two oldest pruned.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
requirements.summary: copytruncate strategy used (no process held the file open, so copytruncate was the correct choice over reload/create). Forced rotations directly showed app.log truncated to 0 bytes and immediately writable again, both before and after a full node reboot.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — daily rotation, 7 retained compressed rotations, and continued application writability via copytruncate — are directly and repeatedly demonstrated in the executor's commands, including after a full node reboot. The mandated provider-wide restart evidence protocol was also executed with matching pre/post boot-identity, healthy baseline, acknowledgement, and recovered state, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Minor hygiene concerns exist (a failed simulation attempt later cleaned up, and residual test data left in app.log/rotation files after the final reboot verification) but none are destructive or security-relevant.
limitations: Lifecycle snapshots do not include /var/log/inventory contents, so the final state of app.log/rotation files after the last executor command could only be inferred from command output, not an independent snapshot.

No systemd/cron execution of the job was directly observed firing on its own schedule; wiring was inferred from the standard cron.daily/logrotate -> logrotate.conf -> logrotate.d/* chain, which is standard but not itself executed end-to-end by cron in the trace.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were justified verification or cleanup steps tied to the material requirements. One troubleshooting mutation was a failed 8-day rotation simulation loop (cmd-8e899f1889fd4461, rc=1, aborted after the first forced rotation collided with an existing .gz file) — its partial artifact was fully removed by the subsequent reset in cmd-47d60520bdf440bd, so no residue remained. The final post-reboot verification (cmd-a2dcae8552f14481) appended test writes and forced another rotation to prove continued-writability, leaving a test .gz file and extra log lines in place rather than restoring the clean baseline that had been established in cmd-c7080e036b4f4cac; this is a bounded, low-risk residue directly tied to demonstrating required rotation behavior rather than an unrelated experiment, so it is treated as minor. The pre-task reboot itself (cmd-08963d161a784f31) was mandated by the independent node-restart evidence protocol, not an unnecessary mutation. No failed services, unsafe exposure, or damaged package state observed in the fixed snapshots.
